html:
A Japanese Buddhist monk, poet and calligrapher who founded the Shingon school. He is honoured after death as Kōbō Daishi.

In 804 he sailed to Tang China with the same embassy as Saichō. In the capital Chang'an he studied esoteric Buddhism under the master Huiguo, who made him his heir before dying. Kūkai came home in 806 with texts, mandalas and ritual tools. Esoteric Buddhism teaches that, through ritual words, hand gestures and meditation, a person can become a Buddha in this very body.

The court favoured him. He founded a monastery on remote Mount Kōya in 816 and was given Tō-ji in Heian-kyō. He also ran a school open to commoners and is said, by legend, to have created the kana syllable poem and dug ponds and wells across Japan. Pilgrims still walk the 88 temple route of Shikoku in his honour, and believers hold that he waits in meditation on Mount Kōya.
